turns.user: Explain why a cache can speed up repeated reads.
turns.assistant:
Cache = keep result close, skip slow work on repeat.

First read: fetch from slow source (disk, network, DB, big compute). Store copy in fast store (RAM, local memory).

Repeat read: hit copy in fast store. Skip slow source.

Why faster:
- **Latency gap** — RAM ~100ns, disk ~10ms, network ~100ms. Cache trades slow tier for fast tier.
- **Skip recompute** — expensive work (query, render, math) done once, reused.
- **Locality** — same data asked again soon. Cache bets on this pattern.

Win only if reads repeat and data changes rarely. Else pay cost (memory, stale data) for nothing.
